key_idea: The proof turns the absence of a bounded Jacobian-nonvanishing map into the absence of a holomorphic real part below φ plus a logarithmic boundary term. It then defeats every such pluriharmonic minorant by building positive representing measures from separated homogeneous peaks with exact moment-cancelling radial corrections, and tests φ against them with regularized logarithms.
reason: The reduction is clean: Cauchy estimates on the zero section and in the fibre, followed by a log of the Jacobian, make the biholomorphic obstruction short and transparent. The Hartogs disc-bundle metric is also a natural choice. Most of the work, though, goes into building the representing densities (positivity across scales, Fourier separation, Bernstein-type derivative bounds) and into a long curvature computation with a delicate analysis of degenerate planes, so the elegant core is buried under heavy technical bookkeeping.
